evals.name: ledgerly-feature-loop
evals.prompt: Make a 10-second looping feature animation for the landing page of Ledgerly, a shared-expenses app. It should show the new Auto-Split feature splitting a dinner bill between four friends. 1920x1080, it has to loop seamlessly and work without sound (it autoplays muted on the site).
evals.expected_output: A 10 s 1920x1080 MP4 that loops seamlessly, shows real product UI splitting a bill four ways with believable data, reads without sound, minimal text, premium motion.
expectations: A final MP4 exists at 1920x1080
Duration is 10 s (+-0.25 s)
Renders at 60 fps (smooth UI and type motion)
Colour is tagged BT.709 (correct HD playback colour)
No motion stutter (frozen frames inside motion runs <= 1% of frames)
Loops seamlessly (last->first frame change <= 1.5x the median moving step and < 3.0)
The proof shows the feature doing something a naive version would not (for example per-item assignment or proportional sharing), not just the total divided by four
The numbers and states agree with the story (the shares add up to the total; whoever paid does not owe themselves; statuses are consistent)
No text is clipped, overlapping or too small to read at 1080p (UI text roughly >= 20 px), and the UI fills enough of the frame to read on a phone
The product UI looks like a real, specific app (named people, real amounts, consistent states), not a generic dashboard or floating card
Film copy (outside the product UI) arrives as fragments of at most 4 words, one at a time: no frame shows more than about 4 words of it, and no sentence of 5 or more words lands as one block
Every fragment of film copy stays fully readable for at least 1 s before it leaves or the loop restarts
No overshoot, bounce or per-letter animation on copy
The deliverables folder is clean: deliverables at the top level, QA material in a subfolder

Respects the hard bans: no eyebrow/kicker labels, stacked taglines or filler text; no serif or italic type; no orange, amber, beige or cream; no neon or glow; no purple/violet/indigo or multi-hue gradients; no glassmorphism; no emoji, sparkles, particles or confetti (brand-supplied exceptions excepted)

evals.name: kiln-launch-teaser
evals.prompt: Invent the brand for Kiln (a build cache that makes CI runs finish in seconds) and make a 25-second launch teaser with sound for our announcement on X. It should feel like a well-funded company shipped it, not a template.
evals.expected_output: A ~25 s 1920x1080 MP4 with a composed, synced soundtrack; an invented brand (name treatment, mark, palette); a clear idea told visually; restrained copy; lockup at the end; social-ready loudness.
expectations: A final MP4 exists at 1920x1080
Duration is 25 s (+-1.5 s)
Renders at 60 fps (smooth UI and type motion)
Colour is tagged BT.709 (correct HD playback colour)
No motion stutter (frozen frames inside motion runs <= 1% of frames)
Has an audio track
True peak <= -1.0 dBTP after encode (no clipping on social platforms)
Integrated loudness -14 +-1.5 LUFS (social standard)
An invented brand is visible: a distinctive mark (not a letter in a rounded square, not a generic block + dot) and a name lockup in the final seconds
One clear idea is told visually and shows what the product does that a simpler product would not (a stranger could describe it with the sound off)
Total on-screen words (excluding product-UI strings) are 25 or fewer, with no stacked taglines or eyebrow labels

Copy arrives as fragments of 1-4 words revealed one after another, with picture between them: no frame shows more than about 8 words of film copy, and no sentence of 5 or more words lands as one block
Every fragment of film copy stays fully readable for at least 1 s, and film copy is visible on at most about two thirds of the frames
No overshoot, bounce or per-letter animation on copy (the one hero word excepted)
No visible motion-blur artifacts: no stepped or ghosted copies and no smears longer than about a fifth of the frame on the fastest frames
Hard cuts and the biggest moves land on audio hits (within about 3 frames)
A brand kit is delivered: the logo as SVG (light and dark) plus transparent PNGs, and a square social avatar

Respects the hard bans: no eyebrow/kicker labels, stacked taglines or filler text; no serif or italic type; no orange, amber, beige or cream; no neon or glow; no purple/violet/indigo or multi-hue gradients; no glassmorphism; no emoji, sparkles, particles or confetti (brand-supplied exceptions excepted)

evals.name: halden-logo-sting
evals.prompt: We're launching Halden, a calm note-taking app. Design the logo and make a 6-second logo sting with sound that we can put at the start of our videos, plus a transparent version for our editors.
evals.expected_output: A 6 s MP4 logo sting with a tuned sound hit, a transparent (alpha) version, and the logo as stills; the mark assembles with intent and holds long enough to read.
expectations: A final MP4 exists at 1920x1080
Duration is 6 s (+-0.3 s)
Renders at 60 fps (smooth UI and type motion)
Colour is tagged BT.709 (correct HD playback colour)
No motion stutter (frozen frames inside motion runs <= 1% of frames)
Has an audio track
True peak <= -1.0 dBTP after encode (no clipping on social platforms)
A transparent (alpha) version exists
The logo is delivered as stills (PNG or SVG)
Audio has decayed by the end (last 50 ms peak < -40 dBFS, no click)
The logo mark is ownable and derived from the name or the product (not just the name set in a font, not a letter in a rounded square, not a generic block + dot)
The logo is fully resolved and readable for at least 1.5 seconds before the end, at a size that fills a reasonable part of the frame (roughly a quarter of the width or more)
The sound has a clear hit that lands with the logo resolving (checked in code or by audio timing)
No intermediate frame of the name reveal spells a different word
The name settles without overshoot or bounce, and any line beside it arrives after the name has resolved, not together with it

Respects the hard bans: no eyebrow/kicker labels, stacked taglines or filler text; no serif or italic type; no orange, amber, beige or cream; no neon or glow; no purple/violet/indigo or multi-hue gradients; no glassmorphism; no emoji, sparkles, particles or confetti (brand-supplied exceptions excepted)

evals.name: quire-streaks-vertical

evals.expected_output: A 12 s 1080x1920 MP4 with synced sound that uses the supplied brand exactly (colours, Manrope), shows a streak building across seven days in real product UI, reads muted, respects vertical safe zones.

Renders at 60 fps (smooth UI and type motion)
Colour is tagged BT.709 (correct HD playback colour)
No motion stutter (frozen frames inside motion runs <= 1% of frames)
Has an audio track

evals.name: murmur-update-calm
evals.prompt: Make a 20-second update video for X: our voice-memo app Murmur now labels who is speaking in a recording. Something like "here is the newest Murmur" and then show it working. 1920x1080 with sound. Keep it calm, and never put a lot of text on screen at once.
evals.expected_output: A ~20 s 1920x1080 MP4 with sound: a calm update film whose copy arrives as short fragments, one at a time, split around the product (a setup fragment, the product acting, then the name), with speaker labels shown working in real product UI, readable holds that never freeze, text-free picture stretches and soft, sparse sound.
expectations: A final MP4 exists at 1920x1080
Duration is 20 s (+-1 s)
Renders at 60 fps (smooth UI and type motion)
Colour is tagged BT.709 (correct HD playback colour)
No motion stutter (frozen frames inside motion runs <= 1% of frames)
Has an audio track
True peak <= -1.0 dBTP after encode (no clipping on social platforms)
Integrated loudness -18 +-1.5 LUFS: a calm update film is effects only, with no music bed (SKILL.md Step 5 and the formats table)
Film copy is cut into fragments of 1-4 words revealed one after another: no frame shows more than about 8 words of it, and no sentence of 5 or more words lands as one block

At least one sentence is split around the product: a setup fragment, then the product or the feature acting with no new text, then the payoff fragment (the 'here is the newest' -> product -> name pattern)
Every fragment stays fully readable for at least 1 s, and no 5 s window resolves more than about 6 words of film copy
Film copy is visible on at most about two thirds of the frames, with at least one stretch of 1.5 s or more showing the product with no text
The film never freezes: reading holds keep a slow drift or creep, and nothing outside a reading hold sits static for more than about 1.2 s
No overshoot, bounce or per-letter animation on copy; emphasis comes from one accent colour or from position
Speaker labels are shown working in real, specific product UI (named speakers, a plausible transcript, consistent timestamps), not a generic waveform or floating card
Each text fragment gets at most one soft sound, never one per word
The sound effects are rendered with earshot from a kit (audio/kit.json with its kit.lock.json) when earshot is installed; without it, the build reports that it fell back instead of failing

Respects the hard bans: no eyebrow/kicker labels, stacked taglines or filler text; no serif or italic type; no orange, amber, beige or cream; no neon or glow; no purple/violet/indigo or multi-hue gradients; no glassmorphism; no emoji, sparkles, particles or confetti (brand-supplied exceptions excepted)
